360	Even if you are small in your own eyes, Shmuel tells him, you are the head of the tribes of Israel.
361	You do not know your own level.
362	That is why you were swayed by the people.
363	"Ah, they brought the sheep from Amalek."
364	"To sacrifice to HaShem your God."
365	"Does HaShem delight in burnt offerings?"
366	He felt that he had done his mission.
367	"Look, I fulfilled the word of HaShem, I killed Amalek," and Purim is coming soon,
368	I killed Amalek.
369	Shmuel asks him: "And what is this bleating of sheep that I hear?"
370	He told him: The sheep?
371	Yes, they are from Amalek, they brought them to sacrifice to HaShem your God.
372	Shmuel shouted at him.
373	"To sacrifice to HaShem my God?"
374	Only the Holy One, blessed be He, wants you to listen to Him: "to obey is better than sacrifice."
375	You, "to sacrifice to HaShem my God"?
376	Even if you are small in your own eyes, Shaul, you seem to yourself like nothing.
377	You are the head of the tribes of Israel.
378	You are a collective soul from the Keter.
379	Therefore they are exacting with you now: "HaShem has torn the kingdom from you and given it to your fellow who is better than you."
380	And He gave it to King David.
381	King David was no less humble than Shaul.
382	"I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people."
383	He lowers himself, but he knows his level.
384	So when Rav Yossef said, "But I am here," what are you shaken about?
385	What, "But I am here"?
386	He knew his level, and nevertheless he was humble.
387	Such a reality exists.
388	What, does such a reality not exist?
389	There is a case of a person who is in a room full of people, and he says, "I am the wisest here in Torah."
390	So what, does that make him arrogant?
391	It is knowledge, obviously you are the wisest in Torah.
392	It does not lower your worth.
393	Another answer, in the way of the secret: "But I am here" refers to the Shechinah.
394	He said: How can you say that humility ceased when Rabbi died?
395	"But I am here": our eyes see that the Shechinah is among us.
396	If the Shechinah is here, we are humble.
397	For the Gemara says, Sotah, page 5a, that where there is arrogance, HaShem flees from there.
398	"He and I cannot dwell in the same place."
399	How many times have you brought the Gemara there, Sotah 5a?
400	"One who is arrogant, even the members of his household cannot tolerate him."
401	One who is coarse, haughty and proud, even the people in his own home cannot bear him.
402	The Shechinah flees from him; he pushes away the feet of the Shechinah.
403	Therefore Rav Yossef stood and said, "But I am here," the Shechinah is present, I am present among us, so there is no arrogance here,
404	there are still humble people.
405	So how can you say that when Rabbi died, humility ceased?
406	That was Rav Yossef's astonishment.
407	But in any case, when Yechezkel goes down to Babylon, after the exile, the Zohar writes in Parashat Shemot,
408	page 1a, that when he goes down to Babylon, then...
409	He sees the Shechinah: "And I am in exile."
410	Who is this?
411	"I" is the Shechinah that is in exile, she went into exile with the people of Israel, and Yechezkel merited to prophesy by the River Kevar.
412	And why specifically by the River Kevar?
413	A place of water has more Shechinah.
414	The Zohar Chai writes: one who lives near water lives with a taste of the pleasures of this world.
415	What a joy to open the balcony and see the sea.
416	It broadens the mind.
417	Miami sits entirely on the water.
418	There are very, very many houses where you open, in almost every area,
419	you will always find houses where you open and you see the sea.
420	The sea broadens the mind, the sea broadens the minds, and regarding what is said about Zevulun, the blessing of Zevulun,
421	where it is written about him the sea, "and his seed shall inherit," so it is written about Zevulun, what is written about him there?
422	"He shall dwell at the shore of the seas, and his flank shall be upon Sidon," something like that, and therefore it is written about Zevulun
423	that Zevulun merited, and he sits entirely by the sea.
424	One who can truly buy a house near the water, it is a great thing; here in Maale Adumim there is not so much water.
425	And certainly not in Jerusalem, there is no water, but still there is a great advantage in it.
426	One who has melancholy, the Zohar writes, go to the sea.
427	Go to a place of water: springs, a stream, a river, the sea; sit
428	there, and see how all the filth is washed off you.
429	This is one of the secrets of Tashlich on Rosh Hashanah.
430	We go so that "You will cast into the depths of the sea all their sins."
431	That the filth will be removed from us.
432	There is also the matter that the sea, in the way of the secret, hints to Malchut, and Malchut destroys the kelipot; I will not get into that.
433	In any case, what we learned from here is that for Yechezkel the prophet, the heavens were opened in Babylon, and that was the greatness.
434	How in Babylon?
435	After all, there is no prophecy outside the Land of Israel; it was a prophecy for the moment, as with Yonah the prophet,
436	to give them hope, to plant hope in them, that HaShem had not forgotten them after they destroyed the Temple
437	and they all went into exile to Babylon, and when He opened the heavens for them they saw all the splendor of the Holy One, blessed be He, the entire Chariot.
438	That is how it was at the Revelation at Mount Sinai.
439	Parashat Yitro, the Parashah of the week: the Holy One, blessed be He, opened for them all seven firmaments, and they saw and managed
440	to grasp and understand what our situation is, what our role is, what our purpose is here in the world.
441	Therefore, this Parashah has exactly 72 verses.
442	Why specifically 72 verses?
443	To hint to you that the name Mah, the name Av, is in Atzilut.
444	It illuminates Atzilut.
445	The name Sag illuminates Yetzirah.
446	The name Mah illuminates the...
447	The name Sag Beriah, the name Mah Yetzirah, and the name Ben Assiyah.
448	When He opened the heavens for them, they attained to see up to Atzilut, up to Av.
449	And therefore in this Parashah there are Av verses.
450	And what is most interesting is that when they reached such levels, He opened the Red Sea for them.
451	A maidservant at the sea saw what Yechezkel ben Buzi, whom we mentioned, did not see; even a maidservant, not one of high level,
452	and also a woman, not prepared for perfection, and nevertheless she saw this.
453	Afterwards at Mount Sinai they merited more than that, and "all the people saw the voices."
454	And what is "saw the voices"?
455	The voice of the Holy One, blessed be He.
456	First of all, what voice does the Holy One, blessed be He, have?
457	Bass?
458	Soprano?
459	What voice does the Holy One, blessed be He, have?
460	A thin sound?
461	What voice?
462	After all, "God spoke with you, you heard the voice of God speaking to you," or "did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the
463	fire?"
464	So, what voice does the Holy One, blessed be He, have?
465	What sound, what voice?
466	I want to hear: what is the voice of the Holy One, blessed be He?
467	So I said I would answer with what the Keli Yakar writes.
468	The Keli Yakar in Parashat Shemot writes that Moshe Rabbeinu, the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to him at the burning bush.
469	And then Moshe Rabbeinu, the Holy One, blessed be He, came to him and said, in what way should I reveal Myself to Moshe Rabbeinu?
470	If I reveal Myself to Moshe Rabbeinu in the voice of a stranger, he will flee from the mountain.
471	After all, how did he even get to the mountain?
472	The Midrash says there was a lamb, a little lamb, that ran away from Moshe.
473	And this lamb went up to the foot of Mount Sinai, "this was from HaShem," in order to bring Moshe to the scene of the bush.
474	And the lamb went up, and then the Holy One, blessed be He, was at the scene of the bush,
475	He kindled the fire in the bush, and began to call Moshe.
476	Now, if it were just the voice of a strange person, you know, what an enormous fear,
